text:
Maya: Hey team — AcmeMaps (org_id: org_54321) is hitting a sudden spike of 429s and quota_exhausted errors since ~2026-03-14T02:30Z. They report map tile generation failing for end users.

Maya: Quick facts from the customer:
- 429 responses include headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 500`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 164`.
- Traffic jumped from ~50rps steady to ~800rps within 3 minutes (bursty client behavior).
- They call our `/v1/generate-tile` route, model="rdw-tile-2.1" in the request metadata.
- They see increased latency right before errors.

Maya: Attached is a snippet from their request log (redacted):

```
{"ts":"2026-03-14T02:31:12Z","org":"org_54321","route":"/v1/generate-tile","model_id":"rdw-tile-2.1","tokens":1200,"status":200} 
{"ts":"2026-03-14T02:31:13Z","org":"org_54321","route":"/v1/generate-tile","model_id":"rdw-tile-2.1","tokens":1210,"status":429,"error":"quota_exhausted"}
```

OpsBot: [ALERT] RateLimitSpike-prod fired: 429_rate > 1% over 3m for cluster: us-east-1a. Incident id: RLSP-20260314-01.

Devon: Thanks Maya — first steps: 1) capture which route(s) and model(s) are contributing 429s, 2) attribute to org/customer and 3) check if global quota vs route quota kicked in.

Devon: PromQL I ran against metrics-store to get quick breakdown by route:

```promql
sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=\"429\",env=\"prod\"}[5m])) by (route)
```

Devon: And 429 rate by org id (we tag org_id on span/metric):

```promql
sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=\"429\",org_id=\"org_54321\",env=\"prod\"}[5m]))
```

Devon: If you have request logs in BigQuery, this SQL shows top models/routes for 429s:

```sql
SELECT model_id, route, COUNT(1) as errors, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM `redwood-prod.request_logs`
WHERE DATE(ts) = '2026-03-14' AND status = 429 AND org_id = 'org_54321'
GROUP BY model_id, route
ORDER BY errors DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Maya: I ran the SQL quickly — rdw-tile-2.1 + /v1/generate-tile accounts for ~92% of 429s for that org in the 02:30-02:40 window.

Lee: Two parallel things we should do:
- Create a Grafana panel showing 429_rate by route and by org (heatmap for burst windows).
- Add a temporary alert to page on sustained 429 > 2% for 10m for that org.

Lee: Proposed Grafana expression (Grafana/Loki):

Metric panel:
```
alias(sum(rate(http_requests_total{env=\"prod\",status=\"429\"}[1m])) by (route), \"429 by route\")
```
Alert rule (Grafana, pseudo):
```
WHEN sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=\"429\",org_id=\"org_54321\"}[5m])) > (sum(rate(http_requests_total{org_id=\"org_54321\"}[5m])) * 0.02)
FOR 10m
```

Samir: We can also inspect the quota manager logs — need the exact quota key they hit (global, per-org, or per-route). Sample grep: `grep org_54321 quota_manager.log | tail -n 200`. If it's a burst window issue, you'll see entries like: `quota:rejected key=org:org_54321:route:/v1/generate-tile window=60s limit=500 count=501`.

Samir: If you want a quick mitigation, I can bump their org-level quota for 1 hour while we investigate. There's an admin API:

```bash
# temp bump +1000/min for 1 hour
curl -X POST https://admin.api.redwood/v1/orgs/org_54321/quotas -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"delta_per_min":1000,"duration_minutes":60,"reason":"support:temp bump for burst repro"}'
```

Maya: Customer wants progress updates. Please confirm before we change quotas. Also asked for advice how to prevent recurrence (client-side batching, token limits, exponential backoff).

Devon: One more helpful query to attribute to model variant (we add model_id tag in spans):

```promql
sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=\"429\",model_id=~\"rdw-tile.*\",env=\"prod\"}[5m])) by (model_id)
```

Devon: Also check our KV prefix cache hit rate — if the customer is hammering unique keys, cache isn't helping and tokens blow up.

Lee: I'll spin up a dashboard now and add panels:
- 429 count by org
- 429 fraction by route (percent of total per-org)
- tokens/min by org and by model
- burst window heatmap (requests per 10s bin)

Lee: Dashboard link (internal): https://grafana.internal/d/rl/limits-observability?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now

OpsBot: Note: deploy-canary job #deploy-812 completed at 2026-03-14T02:25Z, platform release 2026.3.14. If spike correlates with that, consider rollback.

Samir: Quick check — I don't see config changes to quota buckets in the last 24h. Deploy canary touched the routing layer but shouldn't have changed quotas.

Maya: Customer says spike started ~2min after an internal client-side cron job kicked in. Sounds like sudden legitimate burst from their end.

Devon: Ok sounds like org-side surge + existing org quota=500/min caused 429s. We should still create alerting + per-route quotas to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Samir: Proceeding with temp bump after Maya confirms with customer.

Maya: Confirmed with customer — they accept a 1-hour bump. Please do it now.

Samir: Executed admin API call: quota change id=qchg_98765, +1000/min until 2026-03-14T03:32Z. Patch note: "support: temp bump for AcmeMaps during burst".

Samir: Post-bump metrics — 429s dropped to ~0.5% in next 5m window and latency recovered.

Lee: Dashboard updated, created alert policy and configured escalation to @oncall-sre if >2% 429 sustained 10m. Also added a long-term panel to attribute throttles by route/model/customer.

Maya: Customer updated: service restored, appreciates quick help. Will follow up with them about client-side throttling/backoff and token budgeting.

Devon: Follow-ups (action items):
- Samir: Create permanent route-level quota for /v1/generate-tile to protect other orgs. (assigned)
- Lee: Harden dashboard and add a dashboard link in support playbook for quick triage. (assigned)
- Maya: Send customer guidance doc about backoff and token budgeting. (assigned)

Samir: Created PR to add route quota: redwood/infra#4237. Will schedule rollout with canary.

Lee: Added a small alert improvement: include top 3 routes and top model_id in the alert message body to speed attribution.

Maya: Closing — root cause: org-level quota exhausted due to sudden client burst hitting a single route/model; mitigated by temporary quota bump and new route-level quotas + dashboards/alerting to prevent recurrence.

Maya: Thanks all :heart:
